findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and does not normalize input
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks up the email with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison. Signup does not normalize the address (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` directly), so a blocked address such as `foo@spam.com` can be bypassed by submitting `Foo@Spam.com` or ` foo@spam.com `. The existing whitelist/blacklist regex is case-insensitive, making this blocklist trivially bypassable. Normalize (strip + downcase) both the stored value and the lookup value, and ideally enforce the same normalization in the unique index/model.

findings.title: Blocked-email validation mutates statistics and double-counts failed signups
findings.body: The validator calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and saves the record (app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16). Because `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` at line 168 and then `user.save` at line 172, the same email is validated twice, so one failed signup increments `match_count` twice and updates `last_match_at` twice. Any other `valid?` call also changes the stats. Move the match statistics update out of the validation path (record it in the controller only when the email is actually rejected), or make the validator check read-only. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent checks can lose increments.

findings.title: No tests for the moved domain whitelist/blacklist validation
findings.body: This PR moves the `email_domains_whitelist` / `email_domains_blacklist` checks out of `User#email_validator` into the new `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only exercises the blocked-email branch. There is no coverage for allowed/rejected domains, the interaction between a domain error and a blocked email, or the case-insensitive domain regex. The spec also does not stub or clear those two settings, so it can fail if another test leaves a whitelist/blacklist set. Add tests for both restriction settings and set the settings explicitly in the spec.

findings.title: Locally rejected email overrides third-party authenticated email
findings.body: The new `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` check runs before the `authOptions.email_valid` check. If a user first gets an email error (e.g. email already registered) and later authenticates that same email through a social provider, the form still reports the email as invalid and `submitDisabled` remains true, even though the server would accept the authenticated address. Move the `authOptions` trust check ahead of the local rejection check, or clear the rejected entry when `authOptions` confirms ownership.
